messages:
incidentbot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: `canary-latency-prod` (severity: P2). Threshold breach on synthetic canary (region: us-west-2). PD incident: INC1799997777.
kevin: acked INC1799997777 :white_check_mark: grabbing it now.
maria: oncall for this window — thanks. is this impacting customers or just canaries?
kevin: looks like canaries only so far. metrics show a 350ms spike on the canary path, backend p95 still normal.
samira: fyi I saw a small autoscaler jitter ~2m ago in prod-proxy group, could be related. Re-checking logs.
kevin: running quick query against proxy logs:```bash
kubectl -n prod logs -l app=proxy --tail=200 | grep "canary" | sed -n '1,80p'
```
kevin: nothing obvious in the tail, but saw a couple of 500s around the same timestamp (very sparse). grabbing trace for a sample request.
ops-alerts: Incident INC1799997777: PagerDuty auto-resolve detected (duration: 60s) — condition returned to normal.
kevin: noted auto-resolve. still pulling traces to confirm root cause, but initial view: transient routing blip.
maria: any customer-facing errors in SLO or support tickets?
samira: checked error budget and support queue — no customer reports, no SLO burn.
kevin: trace shows a single proxy instance hit a temporary fd exhaustion spike ~20s, restarted connection pool and recovered. stack traces attached to the PD incident.
maria: ok, low impact. can we mute noisy canary-only pages until we adjust thresholds? it's creating noise for oncall.
samira: +1. I'll open a follow-up to tune canary sensitivity and add a short-term suppression rule for canaries during minor blips. Assigning to me: TICKET-2201.
kevin: leaving a short postmortem note in INC1799997777 summarizing: transient fd spike on proxy instance, auto-resolved, no customer impact, follow-up for canary threshold tuning and pool hardening.
incidentbot: INC1799997777 updated: note added by kevin.
maria: wrap-up: handoff to next oncall in 30m — no active pages. keep an eye but marking this thread resolved in slack. :thumbsup:
